analysis:
Reviewed the two CHANGELOG.md head-text units (lines 1257-1644). They contain historical release notes for v0.9.8 through v0.9.15, plus an unpublished v0.10.1 candidate section added in the patch at head lines 11-138. Only the tail of the file is visible, and the patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The v0.10.1 section text is therefore not fully examined. I did not review it and make no claim about it.

This is documentation only. No executable code, configuration, or wire behavior changes in the supplied units, so I found no concrete regression.

The visible historical entries touch several security areas. They are relevant to T-041, SEC-035, TB-011 and A-015 through A-017, but they predate this PR and are not new:
- The SSD prefix-cache TTL was raised to 30 minutes, matching the T-041 description.
- The SSD write budget was raised to 750 GB/day.
- Cache routing persistence stores no prompts or raw chain hashes.
- App Attest protocol 3 only, plus key rotation limits.
- Removal of the unauthenticated earnings lookup (T-031).
- Removal of Python-era wire fields.
- The model artifact revision integrity checks.

I verified none of those claims against source, since the source is not supplied. Two items may warrant a threat-model note if they were not already recorded:
- The SSD write budget increase to 750 GB/day. T-041 documents a 20 GiB reserve and TTL but not the write budget.
- The Autopilot live-control and cached-inventory surface. It is default-off, with observe-only coordinator defaults.

These are noted as unverified contracts, not findings. The next pass should read the truncated v0.10.1 candidate section (head lines 11-138) for security-relevant claims. Examples include page-cache accounting changes to load admission, the logprobs refusal and GLM cooling behavior, and the libs/mlx-swift-lm pin bump.
